disputed: The Aug. 2026 'hunted down' post specifically targeted anonymous government sources ('leakers') who spoke to the Washington Post about a military/Iran-strategy dispute — not private citizens or protesters broadly — though critics argue the same rhetorical pattern (threatening jail for people who criticize or expose him) extends across many targets over time. Trump's claim that the U.S. has 'massive amounts' of munitions was not substantiated with evidence and was directly disputed by the Washington Post's own follow-up reporting in the same piece. Whether the cumulative pattern (100+ threats per NPR's count since 2022) reflects genuine intent to prosecute versus rhetorical bluster is unresolved — NPR's count includes both realized actions (actual DOJ investigations opened) and unrealized threats.

items: On Aug. 6, 2026, after the Washington Post reported on a clash between Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over an alleged missile/munitions shortage limiting options against Iran, Trump posted on Truth Social in the early morning hours: "The 'leakers' of these treasonous statements are being hunted down. Long term jail sentences will be sought!" He disputed the Post's reporting without providing evidence; the Post stood by its sourcing and reporting. (Raw Story, citing Trump's Truth Social post and Washington Post reporting)

This fits a broader, longer-running pattern: an NPR investigation found Trump has made more than 100 threats since 2022 to investigate, prosecute, jail, or otherwise punish political opponents, rivals, and private citizens, including figures like Liz Cheney, Robert Menendez, Eric Adams, and Hunter Biden — predating and continuing into his second term. (NPR; OPB)
sections.label: "Hunted down" jail threats against leakers/critics (Aug. 2026)

items: On Sept. 21, 2025, Trump posted multiple Truth Social messages directing Attorney General Pam Bondi to prosecute political opponents by name — Sen. Adam Schiff, former FBI Director James Comey, and NY AG Letitia James — stating the lack of prosecutions was 'killing our reputation and credibility.' He publicly criticized DOJ official Erik Siebert for reportedly saying there wasn't enough evidence to prosecute James, and said he'd promote Lindsey Halligan, his personal aide with no prosecutorial experience, to take over the case. (Wikipedia: Targeting of political opponents and civil society under the second Trump administration)
sections.label: Direct Truth Social pressure to prosecute named opponents (Sept. 2025)

summary: Trump has repeatedly used Truth Social to threaten jail time and prosecution against critics, leaked-to journalists, and named political opponents — including explicit 'hunted down' language against government leakers in August 2026 and direct posts pressuring his own Attorney General to prosecute Schiff, Comey, and James in September 2025 — continuing a pattern NPR documented as more than 100 such threats since 2022.
title: Trump's Truth Social threats to "hunt down" and jail critics and opponents
